Houlton Band of Maliseet

The Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians is a specific Maine community and government within the wider Maliseet/Wolastoqey world. Its own river, language-project and artist accounts offer distinct starting points; none should be used as a complete history of every related community.

03

The Meduxnekeag and a specific Band history

The Band identifies the Meduxnekeag River as home and describes 1970s organizing through the Association of Aroostook Indians before federal recognition in 1980. Its account connects community institutions with this river setting. Those statements do not map present boundaries or establish an individual’s border-crossing rights.

Read the sources [4] Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians

04

Language work recorded in 2021–2023

The Band’s project account describes language recordings, online teaching, publications and archival research, with specific 2021–2023 references. These are reported activities, not independently measured fluency outcomes. Linked dictionaries, recordings and underlying research materials need their own inspection before further factual claims.

Read the sources [5] Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians

05

Read an artist as an individual voice

Fred Tomah’s first-person statement describes developing his own basketry practice and finding inspiration in nature. The Band’s page supplies an attributed artist voice rather than a universal Maliseet style. Its artwork images and parked external link are not copied or treated as cleared sources.

Read the sources [6] Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians

About — Houlton Band community and Meduxnekeag River account ↗

The Band introduces its Maine community, the Meduxnekeag River connection and the 1970s organizing context preceding recognition. This is a specific Band account within a wider Maliseet/Wolastoqey world.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual About body lines45–51: selected river/place, administration, Association of Aroostook Indians and 1980 recognition account; explicitly exclude opening court quotation, Jay Treaty assertion and membership totals.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Actual selected public ordinary web-reader body independently read by the drafting researcher on 2026-10-28. No access bypass, outreach or automatic permission for linked media. No present border-crossing entitlement, land boundary, legal analysis, current membership total or all-Maliseet representation inferred. Original recognition legislation and organizational records were not inspected.

https://maliseets.net/about/

Maliseet Arts & Creations — attributed Fred Tomah artist account ↗
